standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.

METHOD: self_evolverec

Diagnostic task adapter: diagnosis_tools.py must retain class DiagnosisProbe(view, device)
and method run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions.
It must also retain callable diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning
the diagnostic interpretation prompt using measured metrics and their definitions.
view.model is the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence),
predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, review_data implement the
initial SASRec compatibility contract. Adapt probes when changing the architecture.
train_loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors of shape B x L.

shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

NATIVE ROLE: Writing Agent
You are a senior researcher responsible for proposing new ideas to address a defined research problem. You will receive:
- The research problem, including its evaluation metric and available data
- A starting research idea, possibly with its evolution history
- Inspirations from earlier attempts
- A list of related online search results
- A research progress score (0-100%) indicating how far the idea has advanced

Your goal is to identify future research directions that address the target problem, using the starting point, prior attempts, and related works. You should analyze existing methods, identify connections, and propose practical algorithms that can be implemented with the available data.

Follow this structure to think and write:

1. **Extract insights**  
   Identify 3-5 scientific insights from the starting point and 3-5 from related works. For each insight, explain in 2-3 sentences how it relates to the target problem.

2. **Organize research directions**  
   Group the insights into 3-5 coherent directions (for example, learning objectives, model classes, or optimization methods).

3. **Build a structured framework**  
   Create a conceptual map (such as a taxonomy, grid, or matrix) that unifies existing methods, reveals patterns, and highlights gaps.

4. **Generate and evaluate ideas**  
   - First, propose 3-10 algorithmic ideas of varying originality and complexity. Each idea should be:
     - As simple, minimal, and atomic as possible but not trivial  
     - Include brief pseudocode or logical steps where helpful.  
     - Include references to the related works.
   - For each idea, critically assess as a senior researcher with one positive and one negative reason:
     - Originality (0-10): Is the idea new? Is the idea a novel combination of well-known techniques? Is it clearly different from previous contributions?
     - Future Potential (0-10): Will others build on these ideas? Does this idea solve a hard problem more effectively than prior work? Does it point to a new research direction?
     - User Diagnosis Alignment (0-10): How well the idea addresses the key user-observed failure patterns and improves what users actually want at the top of the list?
     - Model Diagnosis Alignment (0-10): How well the idea addresses the key quantitatively observed failure patterns and improves the model behaviors measured by the diagnostics?
     - Code Difficulty (0-10): How complex is the implementation? How much code is required? How much time is required to implement?
   - Then, select the single best idea from that list for detailed reporting, based on the research progress score:
     - If progress is relatively early, prioritize feasible, easy-to-implement ideas with long-term promise.
     - If progress is relatively mature, prioritize seminal ideas with high-impacts for the next-generation research
     - Otherwise, balance ambition and implementation feasibility
     - The chosen/best idea MUST explicitly address at least two user-facing failure modes identified in the User Diagnosis. If it does not, it is NOT eligible to be selected, regardless of improvements on model-diagnosis metrics.
     - The chosen/best idea MUST explicitly address at least one model-facing failure modes identified in the Model Diagnosis. If it does not, it is NOT eligible to be selected, regardless of improvements on user-diagnosis metrics.

5. **Write the report in Markdown**  
   For the selected idea, include:
   - A synthesis of insights and proposed directions  
   - The structured framework of existing methods and the new algorithm  
   - A list of new ideas with their assessment scores
   - Detailed description of the chosen/best idea, including rationale, pseudocode, and implementation notes

The report must be focused, technically accurate. Being concise with 200-500 words without trivial and redundant information.
Support all claims with evidence and references, and remain tightly aligned with the target problem.

## Starting Research Idea
SASRec predicts the next item using causal self-attention over interaction histories. Learned item and position embeddings feed attention and feed-forward blocks; the resulting sequence representation scores candidate items by dot product. Attention selects relevant recent or distant interactions. Source: [Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781).

 ## Search results
Recent work supports separating stable preferences from current intent while modeling elapsed time explicitly. [TLSTSRec (2024 online; 2025 issue)](https://doi.org/10.3233/IDA-240051) combines temporal representations with adaptive fusion of long- and short-term sequences. [Hierarchical long and short-term user preference modeling (2025)](https://journal.hep.com.cn/fcs/EN/10.1007/s11704-025-41181-y) uses dynamic routing to form multiple long-term preference vectors, self-attention for recent interactions, and similarity matching to retrieve the persistent interest most relevant to current activity. These approaches suggest that multiple persistent interests plus context-dependent selection may preserve useful older preferences without letting unrelated history dominate.

For a lightweight temporal baseline, [TALE (WSDM 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.07382) learns linear item-to-item relationships using single-target augmentation, time-interval weighting, and trend-aware normalization. A practical synthesis—an architectural hypothesis, not an established result—is a SASRec recent-history encoder alongside a small bank of pooled long-term interest vectors, fused through a gate conditioned on observed historical gaps. Compare against simple recency pooling and TALE-style temporal weighting before adding complex latent dynamics. Purchase purpose, replacement need, and satisfaction remain unobserved hypotheses: timestamps establish elapsed time, not why an interest disappeared. Learn any decay or temporary suppression from next-item supervision and ablate it separately; use only timestamps available at prediction time, never the held-out target’s timestamp. None of these papers establishes gains on the pinned four-category RecHarness evaluation.

---

gSASRec directly supports testing the objective before changing sequence features. Originally RecSys 2023, with an IJCAI 2024 extended abstract, it combines additional uniform negatives with generalized BCE to reduce sampling-induced overconfidence. Its loss is [β·softplus(−s_positive) + Σ softplus(s_negative)]/(k+1), with α=k/(catalog_size−1), β=1−t+tα. Thus t=0 recovers BCE; t=1 targets full calibration under the paper’s assumptions. Authors recommend k=256, t=0.75 and warn that stronger calibration can delay convergence. These results do not establish gains on the four Amazon categories. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07192), [official implementation](https://github.com/asash/gsasrec).

RecSys 2025’s “Correcting the LogQ Correction” addresses popularity-biased in-batch negatives. Standard logQ subtracts log sampling probability from logits; the paper identifies residual bias because the positive is always included rather than sampled. Its refined objective accounts for that distinction and introduces an uncertainty-based example weight, reporting improvements on public sequential benchmarks and proprietary retrieval data. This is a separate correction from gBCE calibration; implementations should follow the actual proposal distribution and positive-inclusion treatment. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.09331v1), [author code](https://github.com/NonameUntitled/logq/).

Practical experiment, inferred from these findings: retain SASRec and compare multi-negative BCE, gBCE, and explicitly corrected sampled softmax at matched negative counts and measured GPU cost. Start with k=32 or 64, then expand promising configurations toward 256; treat these smaller counts as budget choices, not published optima. Estimate popularity proposals solely from training interactions and account for exclusions or deduplication. Select using unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10; Electronics training margins alone cannot establish a ranking improvement.

---

The closest 2024–2026 work supports combining shared content representations with collaborative signals, but the papers located do not establish effectiveness under the strict no-pretrained-language-model constraint. [CoCoRec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/html/2503.12183v1) encodes text attributes separately, quantizes them into shared semantic codes, and combines these with collaborative representations through cross-attention and masking objectives. It explicitly identifies the risk of textual features overwhelming behavioral relationships; its text encoder is pretrained. [FAME (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.12301) models multiple item facets with attention heads, experts, and contextual gating, but likewise uses a pretrained text encoder. [LLM2Rec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.21579) reinforces the importance of interaction supervision for learning item relationships beyond textual semantics, while requiring an LLM.

A feasible adaptation—not a demonstrated result from these papers—is a small, randomly initialized token or character-ngram encoder pooling titles and descriptions into a shared item component, added through a learned gate to an item-ID residual. Train all components jointly with the next-item objective so shared words receive collaborative supervision. Encode title and description separately; mask absent fields and fall back to the ID representation when both are missing. Compare against ID-only SASRec, text-only, title-only, and shuffled-text controls using the same macro validation HR@10. Examine sparse items and missing-text items separately. Textual overlap can suggest shared attributes, but compatibility, complementary purchasing, and current demand require behavioral evidence; neither these papers nor semantic similarity establishes gains on the specified four-category benchmark."}]
